# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview

The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and public service decline. It proposes significant public investment funded through wealth taxation and borrowing.

## Health and Social Care

The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

For social care, the manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment, free personal care, improved pay and career structures for carers, and increased disability benefits by 5%.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency, with additional funding for heating systems and climate adaptation.

## Energy and Environment

The party proposes no new oil and gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and targeting wind power to provide 70% of electricity by 2030. Community ownership of energy infrastructure is emphasised. Water companies would return to public ownership.

Environmental commitments include a Rights of Nature Act, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, and increased funding for environmental agencies.

## Economy and Work

The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne, and bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. Regional mutual banks would support SMEs and community enterprises.

Worker protections include a £15 minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and extending rights to gig economy workers.

## Welfare and Cost of Living

Proposals include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, ending the five-week benefit wait, scrapping the bedroom tax, and increasing carer's allowance by 10%.

## Education

The manifesto proposes £8bn school investment including teacher pay increases, £2.5bn annually for building repairs, £5bn for special needs provision, and abolishing tuition fees while restoring maintenance grants. Free school meals would be provided for all children.

## Transport

Public transport subsidies would increase to £10bn annually, with railways returning to public ownership. £2.5bn yearly would fund cycleways and footpaths. The manifesto proposes ending petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027, with a scrappage scheme supporting EV transition.

## Democracy and Rights

Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post voting, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, defending the Human Rights Act, and repealing recent protest restrictions.

## Immigration

The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment policy, creating safe asylum routes, allowing asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## International Affairs

The party supports an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while working within NATO for reform.

## Public Finances

Funding comes from wealth taxes on assets above £10m, aligning capital gains and investment income tax rates with employment income, a carbon tax, and increased borrowing. The manifesto estimates raising £50-70bn annually from tax reforms by parliament's end, with additional revenue from carbon taxation reaching £91bn by 2030.
